blocks.text: Where a customer success manager's day really goes

Nobody has measured the exact split of a customer success manager's day. Treat any single percentage as a signal, not a census. The closest CSM-specific data comes from a vendor survey by Vitally. Its report, The Secret Lives of CSMs from fall 2023, found that 66% of respondents spend a significant part of the working day on repetitive administrative processes. The page does not state the sample size. The same page says 63% wish they had more time for client engagement.

The survey also asked what respondents would most like to automate. 58% named administrative tasks. That answer points at the same work this page covers: notes, recaps, account lists and the search for the right field. Start with the work you already hate most.
What neighboring jobs tell us about email and interruptions

Customer service representatives are not CSMs. O*NET's profile for that job says 83% of respondents deal with email every day. The same profile says 75% make repetitive motions continually or almost continually. The job is close enough to show a pattern. It is not your data, so do not quote it as your own.

Knowledge workers in general get interrupted more. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index surveyed 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets, plus 4,500 more US workers. It says people are interrupted about every 2 minutes during the 9 to 5. That adds up to 275 interruptions a day, counting time outside core hours.
The four time sinks that take most of a CSM's week

Vendor guides keep returning to the same few tasks. Gainsight's AI guide for CSMs gives time ranges for three of them. The guide labels those ranges illustrative and does not source them. Use them as a starting point, then time your own week. The fourth sink, hunting for information, has no CSM figure at all.

blocks.text: Pre-call prep: 30 to 45 minutes per account

Before a call you read the last email thread. You scan open issues, check usage and find the renewal date. Gainsight puts this at 30 to 45 minutes per account. Much of that time goes to reading across windows. That is the part a voice assistant can help with.

Lazur's research runs in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. That suits a company check before a call, such as recent news, product launches or a leadership change. Read the report, then check any date or figure before you repeat it to a customer. Research gives you a head start, not a record.
Recap emails: 20 to 30 minutes after every call

After a call you need three things in one place. You need the decisions, the action items and the date the customer asked about. Gainsight estimates 20 to 30 minutes for a recap written by hand. It also says AI can cut post-call admin to under 5 minutes. That is the vendor's claim. Test it on a few of your own calls before you plan around it.

The fastest pattern is dictate first, draft second. Hold fn and speak your notes at the cursor. Then ask Lazur to draft a short recap from the notes on screen. Read every name, date and number before you move on. A wrong date in a recap becomes a promise.
Account reviews: 45 to 60 minutes for 40 accounts

Gainsight estimates 45 to 60 minutes for a manual review of 40 accounts. That works out to about one to one and a half minutes per account. The real cost is the detours. You open the health sheet, scan the status column, open three accounts that look red, then hunt for last month's note.

Here is a worked example. Say you run four calls in a day. At the low end of both ranges, each call costs 30 minutes of prep and 20 minutes of recap. Four calls cost more than three hours before you count the reviews. Bring that number to your manager, with your own timings in it.
Inbox and interruptions

Interruptions hit every other sink. Microsoft says 60% of meetings are ad hoc rather than scheduled. It also says 30% of meetings span multiple time zones. For a CSM, an ad hoc call often means a customer with a problem. Atlassian's State of Teams 2024 survey of 5,000 knowledge workers found that 55% find it hard to track down information. The same report says 65% think it is more important to respond to messages quickly.
Which AI tools fit which part of the day

Most AI tools for customer success managers do one of three jobs. They write text, they summarize text, or they sit inside one platform and read its data. Lazur does a different job. It sees the screen you are looking at, points at things, explains them and answers out loud. It works in any app that is open. That suits work that jumps between Gmail, Slack, a spreadsheet and a browser tab.

Use a built-in feature when the data lives in one place and the job stays there. Use Lazur when you need help reading, finding or wording something across several windows. Lazur is not an add-in for any app. Lazur has no partnership with any CRM or customer success platform maker. It only reads what is on your screen while you hold the shortcut.
Here is what each capability does in practice.

items: Point: ask where a column, button or message is, and Lazur circles it with a label.
Explain: ask what a formula, a number or a message means, and Lazur answers out loud.
Guide: ask how to do a step, and Lazur walks you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Dictate: hold fn and speak clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app.
Draft: Lazur types draft text where you ask. You read it and send it yourself.
Research: Lazur runs background research in its own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report.
Everyday: timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, and opening apps or links.

blocks.text: Lazur does not do the other half of the work. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It does not send email or update a CRM field. Those steps stay with you.
How to read the sample day below

The sample day on this page is illustrative. The times and calls are made up. The pattern follows the time sinks above. Short tasks come in between calls, and most of them need a second pair of eyes or a quick draft. Each line pairs one thing you might say with what Lazur does. Your own day will differ, especially if you run renewals or onboarding calls.
Gmail, Slack and Sheets on a Mac: what to check first
Gmail in Chrome or Safari

Gmail is where most recaps get written. No primary source confirmed an official Google desktop app for Gmail on Mac, so check Google's support pages before you assume one exists. If you open Gmail in a browser tab, Lazur sees it like any other window. The [Gmail page for customer success managers](/for/customer-success-managers/gmail) covers templates and voice help in more detail.
Apple Mail and Outlook for Mac

Apple's Mail User Guide for macOS 27 covers Writing Tools, which can summarize selected text. The guide does not mention Gmail setup, Exchange setup or a scheduled send feature. If your team relies on scheduled sends, check your mail app's settings before you plan around them.

Outlook for Mac is on build 16.114.4, released November 4, 2026, according to Microsoft's update history. Its release notes from April to October 2026 list a reorderable sidebar, PST import, .msg file support and an option to open new calendar events in their own window. Check your build under Outlook > About Outlook before you follow a guide.
Slack account channels

Slack's download page lists the current Mac desktop app as version 4.53.280. Check your version under Slack > About Slack before you follow a fix guide, since menus change between releases. If you keep one channel per account, a missed notification can hide a customer escalation. If alerts stop, start with [how to fix missing notifications in Slack](/how-to/fix-missing-notifications-in-slack). The [Slack page for this role](/for/customer-success-managers/slack) covers account channels in more detail.
Google Sheets for account health

A health score sheet works best with a dropdown for status, so every row uses the same words. Status typed by hand drifts over time, with one row saying Amber and another saying At risk. The steps are in [how to create a dropdown list in Google Sheets on Mac](/how-to/create-a-dropdown-list-in-google-sheets). Once the status column is clean, [count unique values in Google Sheets on Mac](/how-to/count-unique-values-in-google-sheets) to see how many accounts sit in each status.
Customer data and your employer's rules

Customer data is the part you cannot skip. Contracts, usage numbers and support threads can fall under your employer's rules on client data. Follow those rules before you put any of it into an AI tool. Ask your security or legal team which tools are allowed, and what you may paste or dictate.

Here is what Lazur says it does with audio and the screen. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. These are product statements, not a compliance certification. Lazur does not claim certification of any kind, so confirm the fit with your team before you use it on regulated or sensitive data.

Because Lazur sees everything on screen during that hold, clean up the screen first. Close tabs that show other customers, and hide chat windows that hold unrelated threads. A two-second check before you hold the shortcut keeps the wrong account out of the question.
Mistakes CSMs make when they add AI tools

items: Trusting a time saving you never measured. Time one week of your own calls before you promise a number.
Pasting a full customer thread into any tool before you check your company's rules.
Sending a drafted recap without reading it. A wrong date becomes a commitment.
Asking for a click without checking the menu first. Ask Lazur to point, then click yourself.
Adding several tools in one week. Pick the sink that costs you the most and test one tool on it.
Quoting a vendor survey as your own data. Write down where each number came from.

blocks.text: Dictation has its own trap. Dictated text can drop a name or a figure without warning. Read the text at the cursor before you move to the next line.
How to start this week

items: Log every call and every recap for the next few workdays, with start and end times.
Pick the sink that costs you the most time, based on your log.
Install [Lazur from the download page](/download) and open it. Check [pricing](/pricing) for the trial terms and plans.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask where a column or button is. Lazur circles it and labels it.
Dictate one recap with fn, then ask Lazur to draft the email. Read it, then send it yourself.
After a week, compare your log with the first one. Keep what saved time and drop the rest.

blocks.text: If you want a number for what typing costs you, try the [typing tax calculator](/tools/typing-tax-calculator). It takes your own inputs, so the result is yours and not a vendor's estimate.

faq.question: Which AI tool is best for a customer success manager?
faq.answer: It depends on the part of the day that costs you the most time. Built-in features in your email or CS platform suit work that stays in one place. Lazur suits work that spans Gmail, Slack, a sheet and a browser, because it sees the screen and answers out loud.

faq.question: Does Lazur connect to my CRM or customer success platform?
faq.answer: No. Lazur has no partnership with any CRM or customer success platform, and it is not a plugin or add-in. It works from what is on your screen while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Can Lazur send emails or update my CRM for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can point at the button, guide you one click at a time, or draft the text. You send the email and make the update.

faq.question: Is my customer data safe when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Here is what Lazur says it does. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. This is not a compliance certification, so follow your employer's rules on client data first.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is for macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Gmail in a browser tab?
faq.answer: Yes, in the sense that Lazur sees whatever is on your screen. Gmail in Chrome or Safari works like any other window. Lazur points at things and drafts text there, and you do the clicks.

faq.question: How do I get started with Lazur on my Mac?
faq.answer: Download Lazur from the download page and open it. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Hold fn to dictate at the cursor. The pricing page lists the trial terms and plans.

faq.question: Are the time numbers on this page reliable?
faq.answer: Treat them as estimates. The CSM figures come from vendor guides, and the email and interruption figures come from neighboring jobs and knowledge workers. Time your own calls for one week and use that log.

faq.question: Does Lazur remember what I asked before?
faq.answer: Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac. Check the app for what it holds before you rely on it for a specific account.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to research an account before a call?
faq.answer: Yes. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, and it returns a summary and a report. Check any date or figure before you use it with a customer.
